home.title: Message from the Ambassador!
home.paragraph1: Welcome to the official website of the Embassy of Senegal in Rwanda. The entire team is pleased to welcome you!
home.paragraph2: Opened in February 2021, the Embassy of Senegal, located in the vibrant Kimihurura neighborhood at the heart of the beautiful and green city of Kigali, symbolizes the commitment of the highest Senegalese authorities to maintaining strong and fruitful diplomatic relations with Rwanda, as well as other countries under its jurisdiction, including Burundi, Comoros, Tanzania, and Seychelles.
home.paragraph3: Through this platform, in addition to secure access to information on bilateral relations between Senegal and the above-mentioned countries, you will benefit from a wide range of consular services (entry visas to Senegal, civil status, registration, etc.), discover the rich facets—particularly touristic—of the Land of Teranga, while also following its political, economic, social, sports, and cultural news.
home.paragraph4: The website also provides, through useful links, valuable information on “Senegal Vision 2050” and investment opportunities in the country, as well as on the institutions of the Republic of Senegal.
home.closing: Dear visitors, this website is yours. Feel free to explore its various sections and, above all, share your suggestions with us to help improve our services.
home.signature: Thank you for your visit! Jeureujeuf !!!

content: Head of Mission
H.E. Doudou SOW, Ambassador of Senegal to Rwanda

A graduate of Cheikh Anta Diop University of Dakar (UCAD) with a Master’s degree in Modern Literature in 1992, H.E. Doudou SOW served in the education sector until 2005, the year he was admitted to the National School of Administration (ENA), Diplomacy Section.

He was subsequently assigned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Directorate for Europe, where he served as Head of the Europe Division from 2009 to 2010. He was then posted to the Embassy of Senegal in Kingston as Second Counsellor from 2010 to 2011, and later as First Counsellor from 2011 to 2012. From 2012 to 2015, he also served as First Counsellor at the Embassy of Senegal in Brasília.

Between 2015 and 2016, he served as Adviser to the Ambassador and Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Senegalese Abroad, before being posted to the Embassy of Senegal in Seoul, where he served as Minister-Counsellor from 2018 to 2019.
Since September 2019, he has been serving as Ambassador of the Republic of Senegal to Rwanda.

content: JURISDICTION
In addition to the Republic of Rwanda, the Embassy’s jurisdiction also covers Burundi, the Union of the Comoros, the Seychelles, and the United Republic of Tanzania.

content: Missions
The missions of the Embassy of Senegal, as elsewhere, include representation, protection, negotiation, and information.

The Embassy of Senegal in Rwanda monitors bilateral cooperation between the two countries. It represents the Senegalese State at all official ceremonies and events organized in the host country. The Head of the Diplomatic Mission represents the Head of State and all Ministers of the Senegalese Government.

In this capacity, the Embassy protects the interests of Senegal and Senegalese nationals, negotiates agreements or other forms of cooperation with Rwandan authorities on behalf of the State of Senegal. Furthermore, the Embassy of Senegal in Rwanda provides consular assistance and protection to Senegalese nationals residing in the host country and safeguards their interests. It also provides information on current developments in Rwanda as well as opportunities that may be of interest to Senegal.

The Embassy also promotes trade relations between Rwanda and Senegal by facilitating contacts between business communities and employers’ organizations of both countries. The Embassy of Senegal in Rwanda carries out these same functions for the other countries within its jurisdiction.
CONSULAR SERVICES
The Embassy of the Republic of Senegal in Rwanda provides Senegalese citizens residing in or visiting Rwanda, as well as other users, with a wide range of consular services.
Our services include in particular:
lists: Civil status transcription (birth, marriage, death, etc.);
Issuance of various other administrative documents;
content_end: For any request or additional information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
We invite you to click on the images below to view the documents required to be sent to or presented at the Embassy.

visa.conditions: Conditions for short-stay visas maximum 90 days (3 months), with a processing time of 72 hours.
visa.how_to: How to apply for your visa?
visa.present_with: Present yourself at the Embassy with the following documents:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal or verbal note for holders of diplomatic or service passports;
Valid passport for at least 06 months;
Photocopy of passport;
Residence permit of the country of residence;
Flight ticket reservation;
Legalized accommodation certificate (if you will be hosted by a person in Senegal);
Legalized photocopy of the passport or identity card of the person who will host you;
Hotel reservation;
Certificate of activity in Senegal, mission order, assignment note, or invitation, pre-registration;
Yellow fever vaccination;
02 photos;
Form to download and fill out here.

consular_card.intro: It is recommended that Senegalese nationals register for the issuance of a consular card.
documents: Request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Photocopy of national identity card or passport;
03 front-facing identity photos;
A tax stamp of 2000 FCFA (its equivalent in local currency);
Consular registration form to download and fill out here.
notes: The submission can be done on-site or by email. However, for card collection, presence is mandatory to proceed with the signature;
Only compatriots living in the Embassy's jurisdiction can apply for a consular card.

civil_status.intro: Dear compatriots, the Embassy can establish your civil status documents. Remember to register your family events to ensure their official recognition.

birth.title: BIRTH TRANSCRIPTION - Documents to provide:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Birth certificate (Rwandan, Comorian, Burundian, Tanzanian, Seychellois);
Photocopy of the father's National Identity Card or Passport;
Photocopy of the mother's National Identity Card or Passport;
Photocopy of the consular card (father, mother, declarant).

marriage.title: MARRIAGE TRANSCRIPTION - Documents to provide:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Marriage certificate (Rwandan, Comorian, Burundian, Tanzanian, Seychellois);
Photocopy of the spouses' National Identity Card or Passport;
Birth certificates of the spouses (husband and wife);
Photocopy of the consular card (husband, wife, declarant).

marriage_celebration.title: MARRIAGE CELEBRATION - Required documents for each spouse:
documents: Certificate of celibacy;
If one of the spouses is divorced, present a divorce certificate;
If the man is married (polygamous), present a marriage certificate;
Photocopy of the national identity card of the two witnesses;
Standard form to fill out at the Embassy;
A marriage celebration request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Photocopy of the valid passport or national identity card of each future spouse;
Birth certificates of the spouses (husband and wife);
Photocopy of the consular card (husband, wife, declarant).
marriage_celebration.procedure: After receiving the request, the procedure continues as follows:
steps: Publication of banns for a period of 15 days;
The couple must present themselves at the Embassy, each with two witnesses, on the day of the marriage celebration by the Ambassador.

death.title: DEATH TRANSCRIPTION - Documents to provide:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Death certificate (Rwandan, Comorian, Burundian, Tanzanian, Seychellois);
Photocopy of the deceased's national identity card or passport;
Birth certificate of the deceased;
Photocopy of the consular card (deceased, declarant).

other_docs.intro: For the issuance of one of the following certificates, the required documents to send by mail or present at the Embassy are:
requirements: A request made by the interested party;
Photocopy of the national identity card or passport;
certificates: Certificate of non-divorce, non-remarriage and non-separation;

safe_conduct.intro: This document is issued to Senegalese who have lost their passport and wish to travel to Senegal.
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Photocopy of national identity card or passport;
Photocopy of consular card;
Birth certificate for minors;
Photocopy of ticket or reservation (if possible);
01 identity photo;
A tax stamp of 2000 FCFA (its equivalent in local currency).

legalization.title: DOCUMENT LEGALIZATION - Documents to provide:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Photocopy of national identity card or passport;
Photocopy of consular card;
Originals and photocopies of documents (certificate of authenticity if needed).

relocation.title: RELOCATION CERTIFICATE
relocation.intro: Upon definitive return to the country, a Senegalese established abroad can bring all their used belongings and furniture, and benefit from customs exemptions if they have a relocation certificate issued by the embassy or consulate, upon presentation of the following documents.
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Photocopy of national identity card or passport;
Photocopy of consular card return certificate;
Sworn statement;
Detailed and quantitative list of belongings;
Photocopy of ticket or reservation;
01 identity photo;
01 tax stamp of 5000 FCFA (its equivalent in local currency).

marriage_capacity.title: CERTIFICATE OF CUSTOM OR MARRIAGE CAPACITY - Documents to provide:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;
Birth certificate less than three months old, issued by your Birth Town Hall or Embassy;

Certificate of Celibacy less than three months old, issued by your Birth Town Hall or Embassy, if never married or Certificate of Non-Remarriage less than three months old, issued by your Birth Town Hall or Embassy accompanied by divorce judgment, if divorced, or Death certificate of deceased spouse plus first marriage certificate, if widowed;
Photocopy of valid National Identity Card or passport;
Photocopy of consular card.

family_book.title: FAMILY BOOK - Documents to provide:
documents: A request addressed to the Ambassador of Senegal;

content: GENERAL PRESENTATION
ABOUT SENEGAL
Senegal, known as the “Land of Teranga” (hospitality), is located in West Africa.
lists: Head of State: His Excellency Mr. Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar FAYE since March 2024
Bordering countries: Mauritania, Mali, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, The Gambia
Climate: tropical climate with a dry season (November to June) and a rainy season (July to October)
Vegetation: forest in the south, savannah in the center, steppe in the north
content_end: Flag of Senegal: The national flag consists of three equal vertical stripes—green, yellow, and red—with a green five-pointed star centered on the yellow stripe.
Seals: Senegal has two official seals: the “Lion Passant Seal” reserved for the President of the Republic, and the “Baobab Seal” used for public administrative acts.
Coat of Arms of Senegal: The coat of arms features a lion on a red background and a baobab tree on a yellow background, topped by a green five-pointed star.

bilateral.title: Bilateral Cooperation
paragraphs: Senegal and Rwanda enjoy dynamic and friendly political relations, characterized by ongoing dialogue between their leaders and regular reciprocal visits by high-level delegations.

It is within this context that Senegal decided in 2019 to open an embassy in Kigali, with a resident ambassador, following the opening of Rwanda's embassy in Dakar in 2011. This decision demonstrates Senegal's clear commitment to strengthening its cooperation with Rwanda.

In addition to their close political ties, the two countries are also developing strong cooperation in the cultural and military fields and are considering diversifying their exchanges into sectors such as health, air transport, and the digital economy, among others.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions !!

items.question: I am exclusively Senegalese, can I travel to Senegal without a passport ❓
items.answer: If you only have Senegalese nationality and do not have time to apply for a passport before your departure to Senegal, you can request a Safe Conduct.

items.question: Do I need a visa to travel to Senegal ❓
items.answer: Holders of refugee passports as well as nationals of countries not exempt from entry visa to Senegal must submit their applications to the Embassy. These applications are subject to prior or optional authorization from the Ministry of Interior, depending on the type of passport presented or the nationality of the applicant.

items.question: What documents must be provided for a visa application ❓
items.answer: Visa applicants must have a travel document with a validity of at least six (06) months. To see the required documents or to download the visa application form, consult ► this link.

items.question: What are the steps to follow to give my Senegalese nationality to my child ❓
items.answer: Before any procedure, it is necessary to proceed with the transcription of your child's birth certificate. Once this step is completed, if the child is under 5 years old, a consular registration request can be made.

items.question: My spouse is of Senegalese nationality, how can I benefit from it ❓
items.answer: To acquire Senegalese nationality through marriage, you must approach the Dakar Court, the only authority authorized to rule on this type of request.

items.question: Where to find us ❓
items.answer: We are located in Kigali, Kimihurura district KG 676 ST 44.
